diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We make use of the abbreviation $d_s := d_s(B_{\CC,\bsigma},L_2(U,\CC;\mu))$.
	In our setting, we know $d_s = \sigma_{s+1}^{-1}$.

Throughout the present paper,  we fix  $\brac{\sigma_s}_{s \in \NN}$, a non-decreasing sequence of positive numbers such that 
$\bsigma^{-1}:=\brac{\sigma_s^{-1}}_{s \in \NN} \in \ell_2(\NN)$.

issues.failure_explanation: All three items concern least-squares algorithms with range in V_m (m = floor(n/(20 log n)) in (i), m = n in (ii),(iii)). Any such algorithm has worst-case error >= d_m over the unit ball: testing f_0 = sigma_{m+1}^{-1} phi_{m+1} (unit H-norm) gives ||f_0 - S f_0|| >= sigma_{m+1}^{-1} = d_m since S f_0 lies in V_m, which is orthogonal to phi_{m+1}. The standing hypotheses allow sigma_s = 2^s (then sigma^{-1} in l_2 and the trace condition hold), for which d_s = 2^{-(s+1)}. The bound stated in (iii) then equals sqrt(n^{-1} sum_{s>=n} 4^{-(s+1)}) = 2^{-n}/sqrt(3n), which is strictly smaller than d_n = 2^{-(n+1)} for every n >= 2: a claimed upper bound below the certain error. The same defeats (i) and (ii) for large n: their bounds are asymptotic to sqrt(log n / n) 2^{-n/log n} and sqrt(log n / n) 2^{-n}, both o(d_m) for the respective m. Hence the three bounds are false as stated for general sigma; the cited results (KU21, BSU23, DKU2023) can only hold with an additional unavoidable d_m approximation term (equivalently, sums starting at a fixed fraction of m).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate items (i)-(iii) in the form actually established by the cited works, including the unavoidable d_m approximation term (or sums whose lower limit is a fixed fraction of m); then re-derive the rates using d_m <= N m^{-1/q} in the l_q regime.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:leastsquaresbounds is false in the generality stated (arbitrary sigma with sigma^{-1} in l_2). Downstream results (thm:varrho_n, theorem:varrho_n><, theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine, theorem:sampling-lognormal-holomorphic) use only the regime sigma^{-1} in l_q, 0<q<2, where the corrected bounds (with the d_m term, d_m <= N m^{-1/q}) yield exactly the advertised rates, so they survive once the theorem is restated.
issues.title: Stated least-squares bounds fall below the unavoidable d_m lower bound for rapidly decaying weights
issues.why_classification: The theorem as stated is false (not a typo) for a large class of admissible weight sequences, so repair is more than a local symbol fix and the stated form must be weakened; but the correct restatement is contained in the cited literature and every advertised rate and application survives unchanged, so no major loss occurs.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Hence,	the claims (i)--(iii) in this theorem  are derived from the claims (i)--(iii) in Theorem~\ref{thm:leastsquaresbounds}, respectively, and the asymptotical equivalence

issues.failure_explanation: The first << in item (iii) claims varrho_n(B^q_{X,sigma}(M,N)) <= C sup_v ||v - S^X_{c_3 n} v||, i.e., the optimal n-sample error is dominated by the error of one specific c_3 n-sample algorithm for the fixed sequence sigma. The proof derives (iii) solely from Theorem thm:leastsquaresbounds, which supplies only the second (upper) inequality; no argument for the first is given. Monotonicity yields only varrho_{c_3 n} <= sup_v ||v - S^X_{c_3 n} v|| and varrho_n >= varrho_{c_3 n}, which do not imply the claim. For a fixed sigma whose widths decay super-polynomially, varrho_n can dwarf varrho_{c_3 n} and hence the algorithm's error; the paper's own quasi-optimality relation (lowerbound) is formulated, correctly, only for the supremum over all admissible sigma, not for the fixed class.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the first << in Theorems thm:varrho_n (iii) and theorem:varrho_n>< (iii), or restate the comparison for the supremum over all admissible sigma as in (lowerbound); the rate content is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The near-optimality link in Theorem thm:varrho_n (iii), repeated in Theorem theorem:varrho_n>< (iii), is unsupported as written. The substantive rate statement sup_v ||v - S^X_{c_3 n} v|| << MN n^{-1/q} and the width bound varrho_n << MN n^{-1/q} itself are unaffected.
issues.title: Unsupported comparison of the sampling n-width with a specific c_3 n-sample algorithm's error
issues.why_classification: The repair is a deletion (or restatement with sup over sigma) of a redundant comparison; the central convergence rate and the separately established quasi-optimality relation (lowerbound) survive, so the mathematical loss is minimal.

issues.failure_explanation: For the fixed sequence sigma, the class B^q_{X,sigma}(M,N) is the radius-M ball of H_{X,sigma}; the worst-case error scales only in M. The constraint ||sigma^{-1}||_q <= N does not rescale the class, so whenever ||sigma^{-1}||_q <= 1 < N both classes are defined and the left-hand supremum equals M (not MN) times the right-hand one: the displayed identity is false as written. The factor N enters only through the weight sequence, via the rescaled class B^q_{X,N sigma}(1,1) (for which ||(N sigma)^{-1}||_q <= 1), or via the estimate d_s = sigma_{s+1}^{-1} <= N s^{-1/q} used after applying Theorem thm:leastsquaresbounds. As written, the first step of the proof does not justify the factor N in the final rates.

issues.title: False MN-scaling identity for the worst-case error in the proof of the main rate theorem
issues.why_classification: A short, local correction of one proof step; the rescaling argument is routine, and every conclusion, rate, and advertised guarantee survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $0 < q <\infty$  and	
		$(\rho_j) _{j \in \NN}$ be a sequence of  positive 
		numbers such that  $(\rho_j^{-1}) _{j \in 
			\NN}$ belongs to   $\ell_q(\NN)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For bs = s e_1, the weights (sigma_s) satisfy sigma_{s e_1}^2 = sum_{s'=0}^{min(s,eta)} binom(s,s') rho_1^{2 s'} <= (eta+1) s^eta max(1, rho_1^{2 eta}), since only bs' = s' e_1 with s' <= min(s,eta) contribute. Hence sigma_{s e_1}^{-q} >= c s^{-q eta/2} with c > 0 independent of s, and therefore ||bsigma^{-1}||_{l_q(F)}^q >= sum_{s>=1} sigma_{s e_1}^{-q} = infinity whenever q eta/2 <= 1 (e.g., eta = 1 and any 0 < q <= 2, or eta = 2 and q = 1). The claimed conclusion ||bsigma^{-1}||_{l_q} <= N < infinity "for any eta in NN" is thus false; the inverse weights are l_q-summable only under the additional condition eta > 2/q (then sum_{bs in F} sigma_bs^{-q} <= prod_j (1 + C rho_j^{-q}) < infinity by routine estimates). Lemma lemma:weighted summability, holomorphic has the same defect: it uses the same weights (sigma_s) with an unconstrained eta in NN.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis eta > 2/q to both lemmas and to the dependent theorems; under it, the inverse-weight summability follows from sigma_bs^2 >= prod_j binom(s_j, min(s_j,eta)) rho_j^{2 min(s_j,eta)} and sum_j rho_j^{-q} < infinity by a contained routine estimate. All advertised convergence rates survive with this standard choice of eta.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion ||bsigma^{-1}||_q <= N of Lemmas lemma:weighted summablity,lognormal and lemma:weighted summability, holomorphic fails for all eta <= 2/q. Consequently Theorems theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine (log-normal part) and theorem:sampling-lognormal-holomorphic, which feed this conclusion into Theorem theorem:varrho_n><, are unproved and false as stated without the extra condition.
issues.title: Inverse-weight l_q-summability of the lognormal weights fails without the condition eta > 2/q
issues.why_classification: The lemmas are false as stated in a parameter range covering much of the applied regime (eta = 1 fails for every q < 2), and the repair adds an essential hypothesis plus a nontrivial-in-the-source summability verification that must be threaded through two main theorems; the resulting weakening still leaves recognizably comparable results with identical rates, so it is not serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow rho_j <= 1 for finitely many j. Take bar a = 1, psi_1 = 0, rho_1 = 1/2, rho_j = j^{2/q} for j >= 2, and disjointly supported psi_j with ||psi_j||_infinity <= (1/2) rho_j^{-1}: then (rho_j^{-1}) is in l_q, ess inf bar a > 0, and the smallness condition holds (it does not even involve rho_1 since psi_1 = 0). But sigma_{s e_1} = c_s^{a,b} 2^{-s} decays exponentially, since the Jacobi sup-norm factors c_s^{a,b} grow only polynomially, so ||bsigma^{-1}||_{l_q(F)}^q >= sum_{s>=1} sigma_{s e_1}^{-q} = infinity, contradicting the conclusion ||bsigma^{-1}||_{l_q} <= N < infinity. (The weighted summability of the solution itself is unaffected: with psi_1 = 0 the solution is independent of y_1.) A standard lower bound on the weights, e.g., rho_j > 1 for all j, is missing; with it, sum_{bs in F} sigma_bs^{-q} = prod_j sum_{s>=0} (c_s^{a,b})^{-q} rho_j^{-q s} < infinity follows from (rho_j^{-1}) in l_q.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis rho_j > 1 for all j to Lemma lemma:weighted summablity,affine (and correspondingly to Theorem theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine); the conclusion then follows as before.
issues.overall_effect: The affine part of Theorem theorem:sampling-lognormal-affine is unproved, and can fail, without an additional lower bound on the rho_j; the log-normal part is unaffected by this issue.
issues.title: Affine weight summability fails when some rho_j <= 1
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition excludes the degenerate cases; the method, the convergence rates, and the advertised scope of the affine application all survive.
